title: Model Interop Heatmap & Signal Synthesizer for Enterprise Fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: produce a reproducible, prioritized heatmap of model interoperability (API/behavior/quantization/hardware) plus a signal synthesizer pipeline that ingests telemetry + external market signals to score model substitution risk and enterprise fallback readiness. Context: customers increasingly require deterministic fallback paths (hosted -> dedicated -> private) when upstream models change. We need a repeatable decision surface tying behavioral compatibility, latency/cost delta, and procurement risk to guide rollouts and automated routing policies.

Scope & deliverables:
- Model Interop Heatmap: matrix across dimensions (API surface, tokenization quirks, structured-output stability, quantization artifacts, KV-cache compatibility, kernel/hw affinity). Rows = prioritized model candidates; columns = compatibility signals with short prose rationale.
- Signal Synthesizer: prototype pipeline that combines internal telemetry (latency, error types, prompt failure rates) with external market signals (model availability, release cadence, open-source forks) to produce a per-model substitution-risk score.
- Decision fabric: mapping from score buckets to operational actions (canary percent, autoscale reserve, cost threshold for forced quantized fallback, human review requirements).
- Deliverables: confluence spec, CSV heatmap export, simple dashboard mocks (Console), an initial evaluator harness (not full infra) with 50 model/version combinations, and a prioritized roadmap for automating routing policies.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Heatmap produced for >=50 model variants with documented sources and test prompts.
2) Signal synthesizer runs daily over a 7-day window and reproduces at least one observed compatibility regression detected historically.
3) Stakeholders (runtime, infra, reliability, solutions) sign off on the decision mapping and can identify concrete canary thresholds.
4) One pilot canary configured for a low-risk enterprise customer (with metrics to measure rollback rate and infra cost delta).

Success metrics:
- Reduction in unexpected fallback rollbacks by 30% in pilot customers within first 60 days.
- Time-to-decision for fallback actions reduced from N days to <24 hours for high-risk signals.
- A ranked list of top 10 models with clear substitution risk and recommended mitigation (e.g., reserve Dedicated capacity, add model variant to fallback policy).

Key stakeholders: Diego Alvarez (PM lead), Serena Ito (Runtime eng), Omar Khalid (Reliability), Priya Nair (Solutions / GTM), Kian Park (Design).

Telemetry & data inputs:
- Internal: per-model token latency distribution, error and rate-limit patterns, KV cache miss rates, end-to-end QA evals tied to prompt suites.
- External: GitHub release cadence, model provider status pages, community forks, reported incident feeds, vendor pricing deltas.

Risks & open questions:
- Signal quality: external signals are noisy; need to define signal weighting and false positive budget.
- Ownership: who operationalizes automated routing? Runtime owns execution, Product owns policy — need MoU.
- Scale: producing heatmaps for hundreds of variants may exceed initial infra budget; propose sample + expand strategy.

Next steps (first 2 sprints):
1) Sprint A: define canonical compatibility checks and assemble 50-model candidate list (owner: Diego).
2) Sprint A: runtime engineering to wire lightweight evaluator harness and export CSV schema (owner: Serena).
3) Sprint B: implement signal aggregator (cron prototype) and produce first heatmap; design to mock Console dashboard (owner: Omar + Kian).
4) Sprint B: stakeholder review and canary pilot planning with one enterprise customer (owner: Priya).
